title: Store acid and base reagent bottles in separate containment trays
instruction: Store the reagent bottles: every red acid bottle must end up upright in the red-rimmed acid tray and every blue base bottle upright in the blue-rimmed base tray. Never leave an acid and a base in the same tray.
context: Lab safety rules require incompatible chemicals such as acids and bases to be stored in separate secondary containment, so a spill or leak cannot mix them. One acid bottle starts misplaced in the base tray, as a lab audit often finds.
setup: Table top, origin midway between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left. Two trays, fixed to the table: each a white floor 16 x 16 cm, 5 mm thick, with 5 mm thick, 3 cm high walls (inside 15 x 15 cm). Acid tray (red walls) centred at x 30 cm, y +20 cm; base tray (blue walls) centred at x 30 cm, y -20 cm. Four plastic or glass 50 mL reagent bottles, cylinders 4.5 cm in diameter and 7 cm tall, 100 g each, standing upright: acid bottle 1 (red) on the table at x 20 cm, y -5 cm; base bottle (blue) on the table at x 20 cm, y +5 cm; acid bottle 2 (red) on the table at x 27 cm, y 0 cm; acid bottle 3 (red) on the base tray's floor at x 33.5 cm, y -20 cm.
scoring: Score 0 while any bottle stands in the other kind's tray (an acid in the base tray, or the base in the acid tray), so the starting layout scores 0. Otherwise 1/4 for each bottle that ends in its own tray (centre inside the tray's inner 15 x 15 cm, bottom on the tray floor) and upright (axis within 15 degrees of vertical). Full score 1.0 when all four are stored this way. A bottle on its side, or outside both trays, earns nothing for that bottle.
reset_notes: Bottles are rigid and not consumed; put them back at their start positions, acid bottle 3 inside the base tray, between trials.
fidelity: Bottles are plain coloured cylinders standing for labelled reagent bottles (red for acid, blue for base); no liquid is simulated, so a bottle's mass is fixed. Trays are fixed rigid boxes. In a real setup, colour-coded labels or caps would carry the same information.
